content:
**migrate-v1 CLI REFUSES the real run; a bypass flag is rejected as --no-scrub class — execution gating lives in the C2b runbook order**

What: The `memory:migrate-v1` CLI non-`--dry-run` path REFUSES (points to the C2b cutover runbook) instead of executing. `runMigration()` ships as reachable, fixture-tested CODE — that IS the re-scoped issue's "wire the real run" (reachable + proven), NOT ad-hoc CLI-fireable. C2b wires execution as an ordered runbook step. Design.md Decision 5, PR #220.

Why (doctrine): an adversarial review floated gating the real run behind an opt-in flag/env (MIGRATE_V1_CONFIRM=…). REJECTED — a CLI bypass switch that flips a refusal into an execution is the SAME CLASS of valve C1b already prohibited when it refused a --no-scrub flag (the only sanctioned bypass there is an auditable config allowlist, never a command switch). Execution gating for a destructive one-shot belongs in the SEQUENCING of the cutover runbook (migrate → immediately dual-write → scrub re-pointed), where the ORDER is the safety property. A flag would re-open the delta-loss window: an ad-hoc real run before C2b's dual-write is active strands every later share as chunks-only. The abort-if-populated guard only protects the SECOND run; the first run's safety IS the runbook ordering, so the CLI must not fire it at all.

Where: brain/scripts/memory/cli.mjs (refusal + memory.migrateV1.cutoverDeferred i18n), runMigration in migrate-v1.mjs (exported, tested, not CLI-called). Related: [[sdd/memory-format/c2-migrate-c2b-boundary]].

Learned: "wire it" in an issue ≠ "make it ad-hoc executable in prod." Reachable + tested satisfies the wiring; a bypass switch is an anti-pattern even when well-intentioned.
